sections: Atomic layer deposition of ternary ruthenates by combining metalorganic precursors with RuO4 as the co-reactant †
In situ characterization during the MeCpPtMe3/RuO4 process

figures.caption: Fig. 1 (a) Growth curve of the TMA/RuO4 process at 100 °C sample temperature, showing the /uniFB01 lm thickness as a function of the number of ALD cycles on a SiO2 substrate. The TMA and RuO4 pulse times were set to 20 s and 40 s, respectively. (b) Growth per cycle determined by ex situ XRR as a function of the precursor (TMA) pulse time for a /uniFB01 xed co-reactant (RuO4) pulse time of 40 s [red circles, bottom x -axis] and as a function of the co-reactant (RuO4) pulse time for a /uniFB01 xed precursor (TMA) pulse time of 20 s [blue squares, top x -axis], both at 100 °C sample temperature. (c) Growth per cycle determined by ex situ XRR as a function of the substrate temperature for the saturated TMA/RuO4-process.
Fig. 2 (a) XRR data acquired for the 75 cycle sample from Fig. 1a. The XRR /uniFB01 t parameters are also indicated. (b) EDX spectrum with identi /uniFB01 ed peaks.
Fig. 3 Elemental distribution obtained from analysis of ERD spectra acquired for a ca. 50 nm /uniFB01 lm grown with the TMA/RuO4 ALD process.
Fig. 4 (a) In situ XRF growth curve of the MeCpPtMe3/RuO4 process at 120 °C. (b) Ex situ XRR data acquired on the sample in (a) after 50 ALD cycles.

Fig. 5 (a) Growth per cycle determined by ex situ XRR as a function of the MeCpPtMe3 precursor exposure time for a /uniFB01 xed RuO4 pulse time of 15 s, at 120 °C sample temperature. As the MeCpPtMe3 precursor pulse is of a static nature, 30 s and 45 s exposures correspond to two and three successive static MeCpPtMe3 pulses of 15 s, respectively, while the 5 s and 15 s exposures correspond to single static pulses. (b) Growth per cycle determined by ex situ XRR as a function of the RuO4 co-reactant exposure time for a /uniFB01 xed MeCpPtMe3 precursor pulsing time of 15 s, at 120 °C sample temperature. As the RuO4 pulse is of a static nature, 30 s and 45 s exposures correspond to two and three successive static RuO4 pulses, respectively, while the 5 s, 10 s and 15 s exposures correspond to single static pulses. (c) Growth per cycle as a function of the substrate temperature for the MeCpPtMe3/RuO4 process with 15 s exposure for both MeCpPtMe3 and RuO4.
Fig. 6 Elemental distribution obtained from analysis of ERD spectra acquired for a ca. 60 nm /uniFB01 lm grown with the MeCpPtMe3/RuO4 ALD process.
